summary: Preserve Leaguepedia patch precision and represent missing patches explicitly
context: CargoExport JSON converts text-like patch values to numbers, which loses trailing zero precision such as 26.10 becoming 26.1. Some source rows also have no patch value, while public match-history validation previously rejected the existing empty-string sentinel.

options.label: Stringify CargoExport JSON numbers and fabricate a label for missing patches
options.rejectedBecause: Stringification cannot recover trailing zero precision, and a fabricated patch label would misrepresent source data.

options.label: Consume CargoExport CSV and allow the existing empty-string missing-patch sentinel
Make patch nullable throughout every internal model and public artifact
options.rejectedBecause: The model and UI already consistently use a falsey string as the missing-patch representation, so a broad nullable migration adds complexity without improving semantics.

choice: Consume CargoExport CSV so patch text remains exact, and permit an empty string only for public match-history patch metadata.
rationale: CSV preserves values such as 26.10 byte-for-byte, while an empty string matches the current model, quality-reporting, and UI conventions for unavailable patch metadata.
consequences: Leaguepedia raw snapshots retain a stable string-valued patch field.
Unknown patches remain visibly distinguishable without inventing a patch version.
Public match-history validation continues to reject non-string patch values.

evidence.excerpt: Live validation returned 372 string-valued patches for the current window, including five empty source values, and preserved 53 historical 26.10 values with no 26.1 conversions.
